Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. To move the onboarding forward we need a short model shortlist and a first-pass traffic profile so we can size dedicated capacity and recommend context length.

- Typical expected context length per request (tokens) and % of requests > 2k tokens
- Estimates of peak qps and average daily active users

Hi Grace,

Thanks — attaching a brief export of last week's payloads plus our expected product roadmap for Q2. For now primary use cases are user-query summarization and contextual chat in-app.

Quick answers:
- Features: summarization (~60%), chat/assistant (~30%), embeddings (~10%)
- Avg context length: ~450 tokens; ~8% exceed 2,000 tokens (mostly long legal docs)
- Peak qps: 18 sustained; spikes to ~35 for short windows. DAUs: ~12k users/day, ~2.5k actives/hour at peak

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 3, 2028 at 10:15 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context needs & 90-day token forecast - Atlas onboarding

Grace / Monica — thanks for the data dump. I ran a quick pass on model economics and latency tradeoffs.

High-level shortlist (initial candidates):
- Llama3-Chat-13B-q4: best latency/cost balance for chat and summarization at ~450 tokens avg
- OrcaMini-22B-quant: higher quality on long-context docs; ~10–15% higher cost
- OpenEmbed-XL: embeddings at >98% of the quality for ~60% of the cost vs current vendor

Context & config recs:
- Default seq length: 2,048 to cover the 8% long-doc tail. Use prefix/KV caching for repeated context.
- For summarization pipelines, run a short-pass (512 token) extract then deep summarize (2k) for docs > 1.5k tokens to reduce cost.

Capacity sketch (90-day run rate projection):
- Baseline tokens/day: DAU 12k * avg 450 tokens * 1 request/user ~ 5.4M tokens/day
- Peak day multiplier (1.8x): ~9.7M tokens
- Recommend starting Dedicated Sizing: 2x L4 GPU pool with autoscale to handle 40 qps sustained and 70 qps burst; fallbacks to hosted smaller model variants.

I've exported a short PDF with perf numbers attached.
Attachment: redwood_model_recs.pdf (pdf, 210 KB)

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
